subject: Default capture behavior for interactive sessions and attachments — quick Q&A
messages:
From: Alex Dupree <alex.dupree@nimbusfin.com>
To: rishi_malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Rao <priya@raodocs.com>
Date: 2026-04-01T09:12:00Z
Subject: Quick Q on what you keep by default for live sessions

Hi Rishi,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — NimbusFin is evaluating Redwood for an interactive customer-facing assistant that will accept attachments (PDFs) and run multi-turn, streamed conversations. Two quick questions we need for our security review: 

1) For a typical streamed session (user types, model streams tokens), which elements are persisted by default in Redwood's hosted product? Do you keep the raw request text, the model tokens, or only aggregated telemetry?
2) When a user uploads a file during the session (we showed PDF upload in demo), is that file stored in your object store by default? If so, what is the default retention and is there an auto-purge API?

We're trying to map this into our data flow and show product-security what gets written to disk. Appreciate any succinct bullet answers.

Best,
Alex
Director of Product, NimbusFin
From: rishi_malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Alex Dupree <alex.dupree@nimbusfin.com>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-04-01T11:03:12Z
Subject: Re: Quick Q on what you keep by default for live sessions

Hi Alex — thanks for the clear questions, and great meeting yesterday. High level bullets below; putting Marissa and Kimberly on cc for backup and to attach our retention matrix.

- Default capture by component:
  - User inputs (raw requests/prompts): not persisted to long-term object storage by default. We keep them in a short-lived ingestion buffer for up to 24 hours for live routing and debugging, then they are dropped unless the customer opts into storage.
  - Model outputs (generated responses): we persist model outputs to short-term logs for troubleshooting and replay; default retention is 30 days for hosted accounts, after which they are automatically purged. These logs are accessible via the console and the logs API.
  - Streaming/KV cache (session state): kept only for the duration of the session and for a configurable short grace window (default 2 hours) to support reconnections. Not written to durable archival storage unless explicit capture is enabled.
  - Aggregated telemetry (latency, token counts, errors): retained longer for billing/analytics; default retention is 13 months in aggregated form (no user content).

- Attachments (files uploaded during a session): by default, attachments are stored in customer-scoped object storage with a default retention of 90 days. They are tagged and accessible to the customer via the console and can be auto-purged by policy or deleted via the object-delete API. We treat attachments as customer-provided content and surface explicit controls for retention and residency.

- Deletion/erase options:
  - Account admins may configure per-tenant retention in the console (30/90/365/never) and trigger immediate purge via the Logs & Artifacts > Purge tool.
  - Programmatic purge: DELETE /v1/accounts/{account_id}/logs?before={ISO-date} (see link below).
  - Legal hold: retention overrides for compliance holds are supported via support ticket and require a signed order.

I'll attach the retention matrix and a short step-by-step for purging. If you want, we can run a mini tech session with your security engineer and our compliance team — Marissa can pick times.

Cheers,
Rishi
Sr. Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Alex Dupree <alex.dupree@nimbusfin.com>, rishi_malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Cc: kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-04-01T12:20:45Z
Subject: Fwd: Quick Q on what you keep by default for live sessions

Forwarding the retention matrix and a one-pager. Attachment: redwood-retention-matrix.pdf (table: artifact type, default retention, storage class, purge path).

Quick clarifications inline: 
- "Persisted" means written to durable object storage. Short-lived buffers (ingestion, ephemeral caches) do not count as persisted.
- For customers on Dedicated or Private installs we honor customer-managed object stores and your chosen retention windows; the defaults above are for Redwood-hosted accounts.

On purge API: we also support a scoped erase endpoint to remove specific artifact ids if you want to delete only one uploaded file rather than a time-based purge.

—Marissa
Product Compliance
From: Alex Dupree <alex.dupree@nimbusfin.com>
To: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, rishi_malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-04-01T15:01:09Z
Subject: Re: Quick Q on what you keep by default for live sessions

Thanks — that's very helpful. Two follow-ups from our security reviewer: 

1) For attachments: are uploads encrypted at rest with a tenant-specific key? Can we bring our own KMS?
2) For model outputs: is there an option to disable the short-term storage entirely so nothing is persisted (we'd accept slightly worse debugging ability if it improves privacy)?

Happy to set a call if easier.

Alex
From: kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Alex Dupree <alex.dupree@nimbusfin.com>, rishi_malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-04-02T14:05:00Z
Subject: Re: Quick Q on what you keep by default for live sessions

Hi Alex — quick answers below, happy to expand on a call: 

- Encryption / KMS: Yes. Attachments and persisted logs are encrypted at rest using customer-scoped keys. Customers on Redwood Private/Dedicated may supply their own KMS (BYOK) or integrate an HSM. For Hosted accounts we offer tenant-specific keys managed by Redwood; we can arrange KMS integration as part of our enterprise onboarding.

- Disable short-term storage: Yes. We offer a strict "no-persist" flag that prevents writing model outputs to durable logs. When enabled:
  - User inputs remain ephemeral in the ingestion buffer (default 24h) and are not written to long-term storage.
  - Model outputs are streamed to the client and not written to logs. This mode disables replay-based debugging and some trace-level diagnostics.

Action items:
- If you want a security runbook and a sample BYOK onboarding checklist I'll send both — attaching Nimbus-specific answers file (nimbus-questionnaire-answers.xlsx).
- Marissa: can you propose 2 slots for a compliance deep-dive next week?

Thanks,
Kimberly
Director, Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference
